statement: A uniformly conditioned nonzero three-bank off-diagonal scalar core does not by itself imply bounded density when arbitrary within-bank quadratic phases are allowed. For every nonzero cross triangle a,b,c there is a unique diagonal rank-one completion d1=ac/b,d2=ab/c,d3=bc/a. In particular the unit off-diagonal triangle has sigma_min=1, yet adding U^2+V^2+W^2 gives (U+V+W)^2, whose density is unbounded for iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2].
not_refuted: The full three-large-eigenvalue QFORM conjecture is not refuted; the completed three-variable matrix in the counterexample has rank one.
positive_replacement: Writing the actual scalar core as rank-one completion plus diag(delta_i), sigma_min(M)>=s forces at least two |delta_i|>=s. The next proof must harvest these defect curvatures from within-bank residuals or route them to existing ridge/pair/random-slope branches.
partner_applied: account02/B01 r27 QFORM-CROSS-EDGE-POINTWISE-v1; on the example it yields |phi(t)|<=sqrt(pi/|t|), while stationary phase gives sqrt(t)|phi(t)|->(3/4)sqrt(pi), proving exponent 1/2 is sharp up to factor 4/3 despite three nonzero cross edges.
